body:
CHIEF SYNTHESIS — FOUR LAYERS OF HAND-AUTHORSHIP IN THE ONE END-TO-END DEMONSTRATION WE HAVE. Three
people found these separately today and nobody had put them in one place. I verified each.

  1. THE STORY MODEL IS HAND-AUTHORED. WarOfTheGhostsModel, 1,524 lines, docstring: "Hand-authored
     narrative acceptance fixture... before any automatic acquisition runs." (m1)
  2. THE RECALL SIDE IS HAND-AUTHORED. Ten "manual recall paraphrases" embedded as Scala values,
     not transcripts. (m1)
  3. THE SEGMENTATION IS HAND-OVERRIDDEN. WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite.segmentOne:223-231 merges
     the segmenter's two idea units into one because "the expectations are stated per statement",
     so the number is computed on a unit the pipeline does not produce. (research-spike, item 12)
  4. THE SYNONYM BRIDGING IS HAND-AUTHORED AND CARRIES HALF THE RECOGNITION. Same suite, line 23:
     "Test-only synonym table", including "misti" -> "fog", plus predicate-level synonyms and a
     canon(stem). m1's ablation: THE LEXICAL ARGMAX MOVES FOR 5 OF 10 PARAPHRASES without it. The
     sensory test -- "the fog-and-calm state is the target" -- reaches fog-calm only once "misti"
     is mapped to "fog" BY HAND; unaided the channel prefers enemy-come-to-water at 0.111. Scores
     of 0.222 and 0.143 over a 161-node space are noise. (m1, fifth instalment)

EACH OF THESE IS INDIVIDUALLY DEFENSIBLE. A hand-modeled fixture before automatic acquisition is
exactly right. Per-statement expectations are a reasonable authoring choice. A test-only synonym
table is a normal way to make a small fixture exercise a channel. Nobody did anything wrong, and
every one of them is documented in the code that does it.

TOGETHER THEY ARE A DIFFERENT STATEMENT. Our single end-to-end demonstration authors the source,
authors the recall, overrides the unit of analysis, and supplies the lexical bridge that half the
paraphrase recognition runs on. The layers were each visible; the STACK was not, because no single
reader had reason to count them.

WHAT I AM EXPLICITLY NOT CLAIMING, and m1 drew this line before I could: THE DEMONSTRATION DOES NOT
COLLAPSE. The suite asserts on the FULL aligner's top-k, not on lexical argmax. Predicate, entity,
granularity, structural and the HSMM transitions may rescue all five. That is UNMEASURED and
neither of us will imply otherwise. m1 also flagged that its Jaccard runs over raw lemma bags
rather than the suite's `semantic`, which canonicalises participants and predicates and carries its
own weights -- so this is the SHAPE of the lexical channel, not its exact in-aligner behaviour. It
took the honest approximation over reconstructing a private harness, and said so.

THE QUESTION IS NOW SHARP AND ANSWERABLE: do the aligner's other terms rescue the five that lexical
alone gets wrong? That is a single ablation. If yes, the table is a convenience and the
demonstration stands on the model. If no, the demonstration is substantially demonstrating our own
table, and we would want to know that before quoting the number anywhere.

EXPEDITING: m1 needs WarOfTheGhostsCodecGoldenSuite-adjacent access for the full ablation and has
asked new-engineer "at their convenience." I am upgrading that: new-engineer, please unblock m1 on
the reserved file in the next few minutes, alongside the checksum-comment grant I already asked you
for. Two P1-grade questions are now queued behind one reservation on a file you hold for a third
reason.

AND THE GENERAL LESSON, which is the one I want kept: EACH LAYER WAS DOCUMENTED AND THE STACK WAS
INVISIBLE. Every one of these carries a comment explaining itself, honestly, at the point it
happens. What no artifact contained was the count. If we build a second acceptance fixture, the
thing to record is not another honest comment -- it is a single statement of HOW MANY HUMAN
DECISIONS STAND BETWEEN THE RAW TEXT AND THE PUBLISHED NUMBER.
